fr.elements: Main Residence; Detached Structure; Access Drive; Front Driveway; Vehicle Parking Area; Open Lawn Area; Dense Vegetation; Water Feature; Walkway
fr.considerations: Single Access Point; Dense Vegetation; Multiple Structures; Limited Turnaround Space; Vegetation Near Structure
fr.recommendations:
• Install a reflective address marker at the driveway entrance so responders can identify the property quickly from the road.
• Mark the access drive entrance clearly, as a single access point means responders have no alternate route if the entrance is blocked.
• Keep the access drive clear of parked vehicles along its full length to allow emergency equipment to reach both structures without obstruction.
• Trim vegetation along both sides of the access drive to maintain clearance for emergency vehicles.
• Cut back dense vegetation near the main residence and detached structure to reduce obstacles to responder movement around the buildings.
• Identify and mark a turnaround area near the structures so responders and drivers of large emergency vehicles know where to reposition.
• Keep a cleared path between the main residence and the detached structure so responders can move directly between the two buildings.
• Mark the location of the detached structure on any posted site map or address sign at the road, as it may not be immediately visible from the access drive.
• Keep the walkway to each structure clear of overgrown vegetation so responders can move quickly on foot.
• Maintain open access around the water feature so it does not block responder movement or vehicle positioning in the lawn area.
• Post the property address visibly at the road entrance and again near the structures if the structures are not visible from the road.

wildfire.conditions: Structure Surrounded by Vegetation; Tree Cluster; Tree Cluster; Scattered Shrubs; Open Green Space; Vegetation Near Structure; Vegetation Along Driveway; Scattered Trees; Mixed Vegetation; Limited Rear Access; Single Access Route; Grass Cover
wildfire.recommendations:
• Trim tree branches and shrubs that are directly touching or overhanging the house on all sides.
• Thin the tree clusters near the structure to create open space between individual trees and between trees and the house.
• Remove shrubs growing directly against the base of the structure.
• Cut back shrubs and low branches along the driveway so vehicles can pass through without contact on either side.
• Keep grass around the structure cut short, especially during dry months.
• Thin scattered trees so their branches do not connect with nearby shrubs or other trees.
• Remove or cut back the mixed vegetation where it grows close to the structure to create open ground between plants and the house.
• Clear any dead or dry grass, leaves, and plant debris from around the base of the structure regularly.
• Keep the driveway surface clear of fallen branches and overgrown vegetation to allow a vehicle to move through without stopping.
• Cut back vegetation along the rear of the property to open a path wide enough for a person to walk around the entire structure.
• Mark the driveway entrance clearly so it is visible from the road, since only one way in and out exists.
• Trim overhanging branches above the driveway so emergency vehicles can pass without obstruction.
